chapter: Billy Berg's, Granz and Nat Cole
title: Theme music for Dolphins of Hollywood and later versions of it
summary: A European fan sent him old recordings including the Dolphin's of Hollywood theme, which he recorded several times under new names.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, strange...not strange... But recently, someone from Europe sent me a cassette of all those old records that had gone out of existence and out of my mind. But somebody was kind enough to send me a bunch of those things, recordings I had done with Julia Lee, and my old
recordings of "Dolphin Street Blues" (or "Boogie", they called it), which was a theme song of the Hollywood Music House...
Dolphins of Hollywood. Well, the music they used on the radio program was theme music that I wrote. You might have...
Oh, yeah! The broadcast from the window down there in Vernon and Central?

Down in the window, yeah. It was ...[SINGS REFRAIN] Well, since that time I have recorded it several times (I guess I took a page from Duke's book) under different names. I recorded it once as "Dedicated To The Blues," and I am about to do another record on it with a new name. Mary Lou has done a wild lyric, and it's called "I'll See You Later, So Long."
